title: A convergent series
markdown:
## A convergent series

### Problem
Show that the series

31545\sum_{k=1}^\infty \ln\left(1 +  rac{1}{k^2 + 2k}ight)31545

converges, and find its sum.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
### 1. Factor

31545
1 +  rac{1}{k^2 + 2k} =  rac{k(k+2) + 1}{k(k+2)}
31545

31545
=  rac{(k+1)^2}{k(k+2)}.
31545

### 2. Log

31545
\ln\left( rac{(k+1)^2}{k(k+2)}ight) = 2\ln(k+1) - \ln k - \ln(k+2).
31545

### 3. Telescoping

31545
\sum_{k=1}^\infty \ln\left(1 +  rac{1}{k^2 + 2k}ight)
31545

31545
= \lim_{n 	o \infty} \sum_{k=1}^n [2\ln(k+1) - \ln k - \ln(k+2)]
31545

31545
= \lim_{n 	o \infty} \sum_{k=1}^n [(\ln(k+1) - \ln k) - (\ln(k+2) - \ln(k+1))]
31545

31545
= \lim_{n 	o \infty} [\ln(n+1) - \ln 1 - \ln(n+2) + \ln 2]
31545

31545
= \ln 2 + \lim_{n 	o \infty} \ln\left( rac{n+1}{n+2}ight).
31545

### 4. Limit

31545
= \ln 2 + \lim_{n 	o \infty} \ln\left( rac{1 +  rac{1}{n}}{1 +  rac{2}{n}}ight)
31545

31545
= \ln 2 + \ln\left( rac{1 + 0}{1 + 0}ight)
31545

31545
= \ln 2 + \ln 1
31545

31545
= \ln 2.
31545

31545
	herefore\ 	ext{The series converges to } \ln 2. \quad  lacksquare
31545

### Conceptual Explanation
Factoring the fractional argument into $\frac{(k+1)^2}{k(k+2)}$ splits each logarithmic term into  - (\ln(k+2) - \ln(k+1))$ via [log laws](#node/node-exponents-and-logs/sec-exponents-and-logs-core). The partial sum telescopes to $\ln 2 + \ln\frac{n+1}{n+2}$, which converges to $\ln 2$ via [limits](#node/node-limits-foundation/sec-limits-core).

### Key Technique
[Telescoping logarithmic expansion](#node/node-telescoping-technique/sec-telescoping-core) $\ln\frac{(k+1)^2}{k(k+2)} = \Delta(\ln(k+1) - \ln k)$ using [log laws](#node/node-exponents-and-logs/sec-exponents-and-logs-core) and [series limits](#node/node-limits-foundation/sec-limits-core).
